entities.summary:
The Union List of Artist Names (ULAN) is a comprehensive thesaurus created by the Getty Research Institute in the late 20th century, specifically initiated in 1988. This global resource serves as a vital reference for artists and individuals associated with the visual arts, encompassing a wide array of historical periods and geographic locations. ULAN plays a significant role in art historical research and curation, aiding scholars, archivists, and museum professionals worldwide in the accurate identification and classification of artists, thereby ensuring the preservation and accessibility of artistic heritage across cultures and time periods.

The development of ULAN was prompted by the need for a standardized vocabulary that could facilitate better documentation and retrieval of information related to artists and their works. The project involved extensive collaboration with experts in the field of art history, librarianship, and documentation practices. ULAN not only cataloged existing names but also established protocols for handling variations in spelling, name changes, and attributions, thus producing a reliable and authoritative database that has been continually updated.

The legacy of ULAN is profound, influencing the way institutions and individuals engage with art history. It has become a foundational tool for art cataloging, contributing to the development of other databases and resources in the field. ULAN's impact extends beyond institutional use; it has empowered researchers and art enthusiasts alike to explore the connections between artists and their works more comprehensively, thus enriching the understanding of artistic movements and cultural exchanges across history.
